question: In its Gender Equality Strategy 2020-2025 and its LGBTIQ Equality Strategy 2020-2025, the Commission committed to adopting a recommendation on the prevention of harmful practices against women and girls. A call for evidence was held in May 2022, with adoption planned for the fourth quarter of 2022, yet publication continues to be postponed. 1.
Will the Commission adopt this recommendation before the end of 2025, as failing to do so would contravene commitments made in these strategies?

Will the Commission ensure the recommendation comprehensively addresses all forms of harmful practice against women and girls in all their diversity, including: non-vital medical interventions on intersex persons without fully informed consent (intersex genital mutilation), which all EU Member States recognise must be banned, in the Council of Europe’s recommendation on equal rights for intersex persons (CM/Rec(2025)7)1; forced medicalisation and sterilisation of transgender people, which the LGBTIQ Equality Strategy 2020-2025 commits to address; and the obstetric and gynaecological violence women face when accessing sexual and reproductive healthcare, including the denial of, and mistreatment during, abortion care, which seriously violate their sexual and reproductive rights?
If this recommendation is never adopted, how else does the Commission intend to address these grave human rights violations?
CM/Rec(2025)7 – Recommendation of the Committee of Ministers to member States on equal rights for intersex persons, https://search.coe.int/cm?i=091259488028b934.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.2.2026) The Gender Equality Strategy 2020-20251 refers to harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, forced abortion, forced sterilisation, early and forced marriage and so-called honour-related violence.
The lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, non-binary, intersex and queer (LGBTIQ) strategy 2020-2025 refers to harmful practices against women and girls such as forced abortion and forced sterilisation.

Two of the harmful practices mentioned in the Gender Equality Strategy have been defined as crime at EU level in Directive (EU) 2024/1385 on combating violence against women and domestic violence2: female genital mutilation and forced marriage.

For victims of these crimes and for victims of any crime amounting to violence against women at national level (including forced abortion and forced sterilisation), the Directive provides for a set of rights of protection, access to justice, support, as well as measures of prevention.

Moreover, the aggravating circumstances defined in the Directive include where the crime of violence against women is committed with the intention of preserving or restoring the so-called honour of a person, a family, a community or another similar group.

The Commission is holding implementation workshops with Member States to steer the complete and timely transposition of the Directive by June 2027 (the deadline for transposition). The Commission is currently preparing the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2030 (planned for adoption around International Women’s Day 2026).
1 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and
Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions - A Union of Equality: Gender Equality Strategy 20202025, COM/2020/152 final. 2 OJ L, 2024/1385, 24.5.2024.
